finding.claim: With cache enabled, a token that has exp but no iat is cached with max = now + cacheTTL, so an expired token is accepted from cache for up to cacheTTL (default 10 min) after exp. Expiry is only checked on cache miss.
finding.source: Token presented again after its exp, with the cache option enabled (off by default) and no iat claim (e.g. signed with noTimestamp:true, src/signer.js:96, or issued by a third party that omits iat).
finding.sink: Cache hit returns cached payload without the exp validator (src/verifier.js:377), bypassing expiry.

trace.note: Successful verification calls cacheSet with the payload.
hasIat is false, so the block that reads payload.exp (lines 118-131) is skipped.
maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL (cacheTTL default 600000 at line 499).
On re-presentation, cache.get returns the entry with min=0.
Cache-hit condition: min===0 and now<=max are both true after exp, so the hit is taken.
handleCachedResult returns the stale payload with no exp check.

finding.guards_checked: Cache is disabled by default (createCache at verifier.js:83-86 and :606). The exp validator (verifier.js:304-322) runs only on cache miss. Error caching uses errorCacheTTL=-1 and does not apply to successes. Signature and algorithm checks still run before the first cache write.

finding.claim: Signature segment accepts non-canonical base64url: unused trailing bits of the last char are ignored by Buffer.from(...,'base64'), so several distinct token strings verify with the same signature. Replay protection keyed on the raw token string can be bypassed.
finding.source: Any holder of a valid token; the attacker alters the unused low bits of the last base64url char of the signature segment.
finding.sink: Signature comparison decodes to identical bytes (crypto.js:387 decode, crypto.js:391 timingSafeEqual), so the modified token verifies. Impact lands in the application's single-use or denylist check that uses the raw token string as identity.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE only checks the alphabet, not canonical encoding, though the comment at lines 5-9 says canonical encoding is enforced.
Signature segment passes the alphabet check, so the modified token is accepted.
validateAlgorithmAndSignature calls verifySignature with the raw signature segment.
signature = Buffer.from(signature,'base64'), which ignores unused trailing bits; a HS256 signature has 2 unused bits in its 43rd char, giving 4 variants.
timingSafeEqual on the HMAC and decoded bytes returns true, so the token verifies.
hashToken keys the cache on the full token string, so the modified token gets a separate cache entry and is re-verified; the cache does not stop it.

finding.guards_checked: Decoder alphabet check (decoder.js:10, :41) and the padding ban. The HMAC signature is verified. The signing input and claims are unchanged. Unverified: Node's base64 decoder ignoring unused trailing bits was not executed in this session (no shell) and is based on Node semantics. ECDSA (r, n-s) malleability is the same class but was not separately verified.

finding.claim: Claim validators for allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, allowedJti, allowedNonce, and maxAge (iat) are skipped when the claim is absent from the payload, so a validly signed token without that claim passes the configured restriction.
finding.source: Holder of a validly signed token that omits aud, iss, sub, jti, nonce, or iat. Possible when one key signs tokens for several audiences or services, some without aud.
finding.sink: Audience or issuer restriction (and maxAge) is not enforced for the token.

trace.note: createVerifier with allowedAud pushes an aud validator with array:true (lines 650-652).
if (!(claim in payload)) continue skips the validator when the claim is missing.
Only requiredClaims (lines 293-299) makes a claim mandatory; the allowed* options do not.

finding.guards_checked: Signature and algorithm are verified before claim checks, so this is not a signature bypass. requiredClaims is the documented mitigation. Classified as a design footgun, low severity.
